- When sentiment is consistently negative or neutral in recent history, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for 30-day horizon.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent peak for 10–15 days.
- If sentiment shows strong bullish momentum (e.g., >0.67 for 3+ days), model tends to overreact; apply downward bias of 2–5% to offset overconfidence.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon when price is above 75% of 30-day moving average; adjust forecast to align with 20-day MA if deviation >3%.
- If sentiment is weak or negative for 5+ days, model often underestimates downside risk; add 1–2% buffer to forecast to account for volatility.
- For 30-day forecasts, if last 3–5 days show downward trend, model often fails to recognize continuation; extend downward bias by 0.5–1% per day of negative sentiment.
